# Layout template sources

All templates contain empty city spaces and planned structures. They do not contain source-player names, player IDs or attendance. Internal footprint overlaps are checked. Territory coverage and in-game legality are not proven.

- **LUN**: Caroline’s saved WOS Nerds layout, https://tinyurl.com/2yrcs5ru. 58 city spaces, 2 traps, HQ, 16 banners and reference terrain.
- **Owl**: Caroline’s supplied image-26.png. Grid-traced geometry: 99 city spaces, 2 traps, 91 grey markers interpreted as banners, central 3×3 HQ, a 3×3 node, and four red 2×2 reference resource areas. Decorative blue territory shading and all player names are excluded. Source terrain is a planning reference, not fixed world-map data.
- **Swirl**, **Banner pad**, **Twin swirl**, **Twin banner pad**: geometry adapted from Bleezy-D/Alliance-Layout-Planner, https://github.com/Bleezy-D/Alliance-Layout-Planner/blob/main/index.html. The source README declares MIT licensing. We use layout coordinates only, adapted to this planner’s 2×2 cities, 3×3 traps/HQ and 1×1 banners. No Kingshot terrain, kingdom rules, travel-time calculations or claims of optimality are imported. Single variants contain 50 city spaces; twin variants contain 100.

Research context: Delilah_WOS’s Whiteout Survival layout examples distinguish aligned banner-pad and tighter wrap-around arrangements: https://www.reddit.com/r/whiteoutsurvival/comments/1kgvo84/bear_trap_layouts/. These are alternatives, not a universal ranking.

Applying a template uses the selected BT1 coordinates and retains the template’s relative positions. Roster groups, attendance and the other map mode remain saved. Existing city assignments, including locks, are cleared after an explicit preview. Fixed world-map features remain separate, and blocked city spaces cannot be assigned.
